summary: Adds a durable, revision-fenced release effect cohort and a fail-closed inventory for proving whether retained API and worker effects have settled.

instructions: Run TypeORM migration AddReleaseEffectCohorts1700000000131 before enabling the release effect cohort API.
Do not use a settlement result to terminate retained API or worker replicas until the response reports complete inventory coverage and settled=true.

configuration: EG_TENANT_RELEASE_EFFECT_COHORT_EPOCH optionally binds a managed release process to one positive effect-admission epoch; omission keeps effect admission compatible but makes shutdown settlement ineligible.

changes: Adds release-controller-only open, close, read, and verify endpoints below /api/workloads/releases/{releaseId}/effect-cohorts/{cohortEpoch}.

notes: The new deployment-global cohort table is managed through TypeORM and portable migration column helpers on every supported adapter.
PostgreSQL pooled-tenancy qualification verifies that tenant RLS-hidden queues remain explicitly uncovered instead of being mistaken for an empty global drain.

security: The existing timing-safe private release-controller credential protects every cohort operation.
Opening and closing admission uses conditional revision fences, and verification cannot succeed while any inventoried source lacks authoritative coverage.
No broad PostgreSQL bypass, direct tenant SQL, inferred receipt, or shortened durable-record retention is introduced.
documentation: The managed release effect settlement runbook documents the protocol, inventory, crash and retry semantics, database behavior, and fail-closed limitations.
knownLimitations: This foundational packet authoritatively covers durable plugin event and fixed-schedule work only; engine mutations, Git writes, email delivery, tenant secret broker mutations, plugin gateway calls, configuration reconciliation, and other enumerated sources keep the overall settlement result fail-closed until later packets instrument them.

A cohort epoch must be configured before effects are admitted; a cohort opened after untracked work began is not eligible for shutdown proof. The epoch is immutable for a release identity because covered work rows are release-bound rather than epoch-tagged.
rollback: Stop using the cohort endpoints, unset EG_TENANT_RELEASE_EFFECT_COHORT_EPOCH, deploy the previous host packages, then run the migration down only after confirming no operator depends on retained cohort history.
validation: Run focused cohort service, schema, route, plugin event, and plugin schedule tests, plus shared and backend-host typechecks.
Run PostgreSQL forced-RLS qualification and the supported database migration matrix at the integrated milestone.
